- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) — model fails to capture downside risk.
- Forecast tends to lag in downward moves — true price drops faster than model predicts.
- After sharp price spikes, model overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline — adjust downward by 5–10% of spike magnitude.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights lows — reduce forecast peak values by 3–5% for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecasts with 3-day moving average.
- For 30d horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window — reduce first 5–7 days by 2–4% to align with true price decay.
